implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: a flat array holding a complete binary tree, where the parent of i is (i-1)/2 and the children of i are 2i+1 and 2i+2. Maintain the invariant that the parent dominates both children. Insert appends at the end and sifts up; remove takes the root, moves the last element to the root, and sifts down, always promoting the smaller child so the sibling side is not violated. peek is a[0]. Build from an existing array by sift-down from the last internal node to the root - Floyd's linear construction. Use hole-punching rather than swapping (one write per level). Add a monotonic counter as a secondary key for stable ordering among equals, and an index map if you need decrease-key.
idiom_name: binary heap in a flat array with sift-up / sift-down and Floyd's O(n) heapify
pitfalls: Sift-down must promote the smaller child; promoting the larger creates a fresh violation on the sibling side and corrupts silently.
Guard i > 0 before computing the parent: on an unsigned type (0-1)/2 wraps to a huge index rather than -1.
Bounds-check the right child before reading it - the last internal node often has only a left child.
The root is only guaranteed after a valid sift; 'it looks sorted' is not an invariant check.
